liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Cryptical Envelopement** (2 reviews): Reviewer calls the Cryptical into The Other One sequence intense; Reviewer says the Cryptical reprise evokes a psychedelic trip [7][12]
- **Uncle John's Band** (2 reviews): Reviewer especially likes the early arrangement of Uncle John's Band, along with Dire Wolf and Black Peter; Listener hears what may be a banjo and possibly a mandolin in Uncle John's Band [9][18]
- **Dancin' In The Streets** (2 reviews): Reviewer finds Dancin' and the other lower-quality-source tracks superb [16][17]
- **It's All Over Now Baby Blue** (2 reviews): Baby Blue foreshadows the band's later musical heights, but played differently from the 1980s and 90s [16][17]
- **Big Boy Pete** (1 review): Reviewer likes this Big Boy Pete, though thinks it falls short of the September 1970 version [10]
- **Hard To Handle** (1 review): Reviewer is lukewarm on Hard To Handle apart from a groovy scat bit by Pigpen [10]
- **Good Lovin'** (1 review): Reviewer singles out Good Lovin' and its drums segment as lovely [7]
- **Cumberland Blues** (1 review): Reviewer judges Cumberland Blues probably the best performance of the night [14]

## Setlist highlights

- **Big Boy Pete**: rare: 11 archived performances [19]

## The recordings

- **gd70-03-01.sbd.hanno.4641.sbefail.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 23 songs; 135 min; rated 3.78/5 by 9 [1]. Said about its sound: Quality is good except the first two tracks and the final two tracks; First two songs and part of Big Boy Pete come from poor microphone audience recording; the rest is a soundboard; Soundboard portion is excellent, though Garcia's guitar could be slightly higher in the mix [7][8][9][10][11][16]
- **gd1970-03-01.176244.aud.ely.terry.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 23 songs; 115 min [2]. Said about its sound: Most songs are clipped at the start [2]
- **gd1970-03-01.136666.sbd.sirmick.flac16**: soundboard; 19 songs; 110 min; rated 4.5/5 by 2 [5]. Said about its sound: Very clear recording, vocals a bit high in the mix and needing EQ; two sources are used [17]
- **gd1970-03-01.sbd.ben.91.shnf**: soundboard; 17 songs; 110 min; rated 4.67/5 by 3 [6]. Said about its sound: Described as an excellent soundboard [12]

## Around the show

- The venue building still stands, though it no longer carries the Great Highway name [11]
- Feedback during The Other One apparently forced the band to turn down, leaving the rest mellower [14]
- Reviewer wouldn't start with this show for 1970 Dead; performance is good but somewhat sloppy [9]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd70-03-01.sbd.hanno.4641.sbefail.shnf**: transferred by Hanno Bunjes, Uli T, Matjaz; source: Soundboard [1]. Also: Soundboard patched with audience recording by Hanno Bunjes, from a third-generation cassette, speed-corrected and amplified in SoundForge [1]
- **gd1970-03-01.176244.aud.ely.terry.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Harry Ely, Mark Terry; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Harry Ely's Audience Master (unknown equipment) > 1st Generation Cassette > Mark Terry's 2nd Generation Cassette (Maxell UD XLII-C90, no dolby) [2]
- **gd1970-03-01.136666.sbd.sirmick.flac16**: taped by Anonomous; transferred by SIRMick; source: Source: Soundboard > Mater Reel > Dat (44.1k) [5]
- **gd1970-03-01.sbd.ben.91.shnf**: transferred by Ben; source: S:MR>C>D>CDR [6]. Also: Soundboard has a reel splice at 5:29 of King Bee [6]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Randy Tuten: [12 | October | 2019 | Original Concert Posters](https://original-concert-posters.com/2019/10/12/) [20]
